title: Does Vitamin C Neutralize Chlorine? What the Science Says (and Where It Falls Short)
excerpt: Yes, vitamin C reacts with free chlorine and turns it into harmless chloride. Here is what is well established, what is not, and how to test your own water.
author: Aroma Sense
bodyHtml:
Short answer: yes. Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) reacts with free chlorine in water and converts it into harmless chloride. Water system operators use the same chemistry to dechlorinate water. The harder question, and the one that matters for a shower filter, is whether it works fast enough, for long enough, and on the kind of disinfectant in your water. This guide covers what is well established, what is not, and how to check for yourself.

We make vitamin C shower filters, so we have an interest in this topic. Our sources are linked at the end, and we have tried to say plainly where the evidence stops.

How vitamin C neutralizes chlorine

Chlorine added to drinking water is an oxidizer, which is what makes it kill germs. Vitamin C is a reducing agent, meaning it readily gives up electrons. When the two meet, the chlorine is reduced to chloride (the same ion found in table salt) and the vitamin C is oxidized to dehydroascorbic acid. Nothing is physically filtered out. The chlorine is chemically converted into something else.

A technical report from the U.S. Forest Service's San Dimas Technology and Development Center, written for water system operators, describes the reaction as very fast. Its working ratio is roughly 2.5 parts of ascorbic acid to neutralize 1 part of chlorine by weight. The same report notes that most of the studies it reviewed looked at low chlorine levels, below 2 mg/L.

Does vitamin C remove chlorine from tap water?

For free chlorine, yes. That is the established part. The CDC considers chlorine or chloramine levels up to 4 mg/L safe in drinking water. The exact number in your home depends on your utility and how far your tap is from the treatment plant, and your utility publishes it in its annual water quality report.

What the chemistry does not tell you is how a small cartridge performs in a shower. Water passes through it in seconds, at your shower's flow rate, and the vitamin C is gradually used up. That is a design and durability question that varies from product to product.

Free chlorine versus chloramine: the caveat that matters

Many water utilities disinfect with chloramine (chlorine combined with ammonia) instead of free chlorine. Both the EPA and the CDC note that chloramine provides longer-lasting disinfection as water moves through the pipes, which is why some utilities switch to it. In general chemistry terms, a disinfectant that persists is also one that reacts more slowly, and a shower cartridge only gets a few seconds of contact with the water.

We are not aware of published independent testing of shower cartridges against chloramine at real shower flow rates. So if your water is chloraminated, treat any vendor claim, including ours, with extra caution and test it yourself (see below). Our product pages describe chlorine neutralization. They do not make claims about chloramine.

Does vitamin C neutralize chlorine on skin or hair?

The vitamin C in a shower filter treats the water before it reaches you. That is different from putting vitamin C on your skin or hair after exposure, and we are not aware of solid evidence either way for that second case. If you have been swimming, the standard dermatology advice is to rinse and moisturize.

Why reduce chlorine in your shower at all?

Dermatologist Dr. Jennifer Lucas of Cleveland Clinic describes chlorine as very drying to hair and skin, and notes it can make hair more brittle and cause irritant contact dermatitis. That advice is about pool water, which involves longer exposure than a shower. Evidence specifically on tap-water chlorine in a ten-minute shower is thinner.

So we will not tell you a filter treats any skin or hair condition, because that would go beyond the evidence. If your skin or hair feels dry and you would like to try cutting chlorine exposure, it is a low-risk experiment. If you have eczema or another skin condition, ask your dermatologist first.

What a vitamin C shower filter does not do

  • It does not soften hard water. Hardness comes from calcium and magnesium, which vitamin C does not remove. See our guide to shower filters and hard water.
  • It is not a general purifier. The vitamin C cartridge targets chlorine. In Aroma Sense heads, a separate microfiber filter traps sediment, rust and dirt from your pipes.
  • It does not last forever. A spent cartridge does nothing. Our cartridge pages say to replace them within roughly 30 to 45 days depending on scent and usage.

How to check whether your filter is working

  1. Find out what your utility uses. Your annual water quality report (also called a Consumer Confidence Report) says whether your water is disinfected with chlorine or chloramine.
  2. Test before and after. A DPD-based free chlorine test kit, sold for pools and aquariums, lets you compare water from your tap with water that has passed through the filter. Some inexpensive pool strips are not sensitive enough for tap-water levels, so a drop-test kit is more reliable.
  3. Replace cartridges on schedule. Note the install date on your calendar.

The bottom line

Vitamin C does neutralize free chlorine, and that chemistry is well documented. Whether a particular shower cartridge does it well in your bathroom depends on the design, the cartridge's age, and whether your water uses free chlorine or chloramine. If you would like to see how ours works, read how an Aroma Sense shower head works, browse the shower heads, or find replacement vitamin C cartridges. For a broader look, see Do Shower Filters Really Work?

Sources

  • Using Vitamin C to Neutralize Chlorine in Water Systems, U.S. Forest Service, San Dimas Technology and Development Center (2005)
  • Chloramines in Drinking Water, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency
  • About Water Disinfection with Chlorine and Chloramine, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
  • Does Pool Water Affect Your Skin and Hair?, Cleveland Clinic (2024)

title: Shower Filter for Hard Water: What Actually Works (and What Doesn't)
excerpt: Most shower filters, including vitamin C ones, do not remove the calcium and magnesium that make water hard. Here is what does, and where filters help.
author: Aroma Sense
bodyHtml:
Short answer: most shower filters, including vitamin C filters like ours, are not designed to remove the calcium and magnesium that make water hard. What actually reduces hardness is a water softener. Shower filters solve a different problem: chlorine and sediment. Many homes have both issues, so it helps to know which tool does which job.

We sell vitamin C shower filters, and we would rather you buy the right product for your water than the wrong one from us. Our sources are linked at the end.

What hard water is

The U.S. Geological Survey defines water hardness simply as the amount of dissolved calcium and magnesium in the water. It is measured in milligrams per liter as calcium carbonate, and the USGS uses these ranges:

  • Soft: 0 to 60 mg/L
  • Moderately hard: 61 to 120 mg/L
  • Hard: 121 to 180 mg/L
  • Very hard: over 180 mg/L

Some reports use grains per gallon instead. One grain per gallon equals about 17.1 mg/L.

Is hard water bad for you?

According to the USGS, hardness is not a health concern, but it can be a nuisance. Hard water reacts with soap to form soap scum, so you need more soap or detergent. When hard water is heated, calcium carbonate deposits (scale) can form. Scale can reduce the life of equipment, make heating water less efficient, and gradually narrow pipes, which reduces flow and pressure.

That last point is why hard water shows up in showers: white crust on fixtures, a film on glass, and spray holes that clog over time.

Will a shower filter fix hard water?

Generally, no. A vitamin C cartridge targets chlorine, and a microfiber filter traps sediment, rust and dirt. Neither is designed to remove calcium or magnesium. That is true of the Aroma Sense filters, and it is true of most shower filters on the market, whatever the marketing implies.

This is worth knowing if you searched for a "vitamin C shower filter for hard water". Vitamin C and hard water are two separate topics. A vitamin C filter can still be useful if you also want less chlorine, but it will not stop scale.

What does reduce hardness

The proven approach is a salt-based ion exchange water softener, usually installed on the water line for the whole home. According to the EPA's WaterSense program, these softeners remove calcium and magnesium by exchanging them with sodium (or potassium) ions. The resin has to be regenerated periodically, and the EPA notes that regeneration can use 25 gallons of water or more per day, or up to 10,000 gallons per year.

Softeners come with trade-offs worth weighing: an upfront cost, water use for regeneration, and the fact that the minerals are swapped for sodium or potassium, so a little of it ends up in the treated water. They also address minerals, not chlorine, so they do a different job from a shower filter.

What about hair and skin?

Because hard water reacts with soap to form scum, it can leave a film and change how cleansers lather and rinse. That is one reason people report their hair or skin feeling different in hard water. Rigorous evidence for lasting hair or skin damage is thinner than product marketing suggests, so we will not promise that a softener or a filter will fix a specific hair or skin problem. If you have a skin condition, ask a dermatologist.

How to find out how hard your water is

  1. Check your water quality report. Utilities publish one every year, and some include hardness. Your utility can tell you if yours does not.
  2. Use a hardness test strip. Inexpensive strips report hardness in mg/L or grains per gallon.
  3. Look for signs. White crust on faucets, cloudy glassware and clogged spray holes point to hard water.

Where a vitamin C shower filter still fits

If your water is both hard and chlorinated, a softener and a shower filter do different jobs and can work together. Read Does Vitamin C Neutralize Chlorine? to see what a vitamin C filter does and does not do. To see how our shower heads are built, read how an Aroma Sense shower head works, or browse the shower heads and vitamin C cartridges.

Sources

  • Hardness of Water, U.S. Geological Survey Water Science School
  • Cation Exchange Water Softeners, U.S. EPA WaterSense

Do Shower Filters Really Work? Here’s the Science Explained

Posted by Matthew Eng on April 30, 2026

And why Aroma Sense is engineered to make a real difference

If you’ve ever wondered whether shower filters are just hype or actually effective, you’re not alone. With so many products on the market, it’s fair to ask: Do shower filters really work?

The short answer: Yes—when they’re designed correctly and use the right filtration technology.
Let’s break down the science behind it—and where most basic filters fall short.

🚿 What’s in Your Shower Water?

Before understanding filtration, it helps to know what you’re filtering out.

Even treated municipal water can contain:

  • Chlorine & chloramines (used for disinfection)
  • Heavy metals (trace amounts from aging pipes)
  • Sediment & rust particles
  • Hard water minerals (calcium & magnesium)

These aren’t always dangerous to drink—but they can be harsh on your skin and hair, especially with daily exposure.

🔬 How Shower Filters Actually Work

At a scientific level, shower filters use physical and chemical filtration to reduce impurities.

1. Physical Filtration (Sediment Removal)

  • Mesh or microfiber layers trap particles like rust, sand, and debris
  • Improves water clarity and prevents buildup on skin and hair

2. Chemical Filtration (Neutralizing Chlorine)

  • Advanced media like Vitamin C or KDF (copper-zinc alloy) react with chlorine
  • This reaction converts chlorine into harmless compounds

👉 This is key because chlorine is one of the biggest contributors to dryness and irritation.

3. Mineral Conditioning

  • Some systems include mineral elements that help reduce the harsh effects of hard water
  • This doesn’t fully soften water like a whole-home system, but it improves feel and manageability

⚠️ Why Basic Shower Filters Often Fall Short

Many low-cost filters on the market:

  • Use minimal filtration media
  • Have poor water contact time (water flows too quickly to be treated)
  • Struggle to neutralize chlorine in hot water
  • Focus more on marketing than real performance

That’s why some people try a cheap filter and think, “This didn’t do anything.”

In many cases, the issue isn’t the concept—it’s the quality of the filter.

🌊 Where Aroma Sense Stands Out

This is where Aroma Sense separates itself from generic shower filters.

💡 1. Advanced Vitamin C Filtration

Aroma Sense systems use Vitamin C cartridges, which are highly effective because:

  • They neutralize chlorine instantly—even at high temperatures
  • They help reduce harsh chemical exposure on skin and hair
  • They support a more gentle, skin-friendly water experience

🚿 2. Optimized Water Pressure + Filtration Balance

Unlike bulky filters that reduce pressure, Aroma Sense designs maintain:

  • Strong, consistent water flow
  • Proper contact time for filtration
  • A more satisfying, spa-like shower experience

🌸 3. Aromatherapy + Wellness Integration

Aroma Sense goes beyond filtration by combining:

  • Clean, filtered water
  • Light aromatherapy infusion
  • A more relaxing, elevated daily routine

This transforms your shower from a basic necessity into a wellness ritual.

💆 Real Benefits You Can Actually Feel

When a shower filter works properly, the results are noticeable:

Skin

  • Less dryness and tightness
  • Reduced irritation
  • Softer, more hydrated feel

Hair

  • Less brittleness
  • Improved shine and smoothness
  • Healthier scalp environment

Overall Experience

  • Cleaner-feeling water
  • More enjoyable showers
  • Reduced chemical smell

🧠 The Bottom Line: Do Shower Filters Work?

Yes—but only if they’re engineered properly.

The science is real:

  • Chlorine can be neutralized
  • Sediment can be removed
  • Water quality can be improved

However, the effectiveness depends entirely on the system you use.

✨ Why It Matters for Your Daily Routine

You shower almost every day. That means your skin and hair are constantly exposed to your water quality.

Upgrading to a high-quality filtered system—like those from Aroma Sense—is one of the simplest ways to:

  • Improve how your skin feels
  • Get better results from your hair and skincare products
  • Elevate a routine you already do daily

Final Thoughts

Shower filters aren’t a gimmick—they’re a science-backed upgrade to your everyday life.

The difference comes down to quality, technology, and design.

With the right system, you’re not just filtering water—you’re improving your skin, hair, and overall experience every single day.

The Benefits of Showering with Clean, Filtered Water

Posted by Matthew Eng on April 30, 2026

Why upgrading your shower water is one of the simplest ways to improve your skin, hair, and overall wellness

When people think about improving their health, they often focus on diet, exercise, or skincare products—but one major factor is usually overlooked: the quality of your shower water.

Every day, your skin and hair are exposed to whatever is in your tap water. While it may be safe to drink, it’s not always ideal for your body externally. That’s where clean, filtered shower water comes in.

Let’s break down why making the switch can be a game-changer.

🚿 What’s Really in Your Shower Water?

Municipal water systems use disinfectants like chlorine to kill bacteria and keep water safe. While effective for sanitation, these chemicals—and other impurities—can have unintended effects on your skin and hair.

Common contaminants include:

  • Chlorine and chloramines
  • Heavy metals (like lead or mercury in trace amounts)
  • Sediment and rust
  • Hard water minerals (calcium and magnesium)

Over time, exposure to these elements can lead to dryness, irritation, and buildup.

🌿 1. Healthier, More Hydrated Skin

Filtered water helps remove harsh chemicals that strip your skin of its natural oils.

Benefits:

  • Reduced dryness and flakiness
  • Less irritation for sensitive skin
  • Improved skin barrier function
  • Softer, smoother texture

If you’ve ever stepped out of the shower feeling tight or itchy, your water may be part of the problem—not your soap.

💆 2. Stronger, Shinier Hair

Unfiltered water can leave behind mineral deposits and chemical residue that damage your hair over time.

With filtered water, you may notice:

  • Less dryness and brittleness
  • Improved shine and softness
  • Reduced scalp irritation
  • Better results from shampoos and conditioners

Filtered water allows your hair care products to actually do their job—without interference from buildup.

🧴 3. Better Absorption of Skincare & Haircare Products

When your skin and hair are coated with chlorine or minerals, they can’t properly absorb nutrients from your products.

Clean water helps:

  • Enhance the effectiveness of moisturizers
  • Improve absorption of serums and treatments
  • Reduce the need for excessive product use

In other words, you get more value out of everything you already use.

bodyHtml:
Aromatherapy for Anxiety

Posted by Matthew Eng on September 21, 2022

Throughout our nation, we continue to face uncertain times, making stress and anxiety harder to cope with. Various negative effects can be caused by long-term stress on the body, both physically and mentally. 

It's not surprising that long-term stress can cause anxiety, irritability, anger, headaches, sleeping issues, digestive issues, and chest pain, according to the Mayo Clinic. 

Many individuals are using holistic approaches to combat stress, such as aromatherapy, as well as traditional remedies like exercising and counseling. 

Essential oils are extracted from plants that are either inhaled or applied to the skin in this kind of treatment. While getting a massage or taking a bath, some people apply the oils to their skin.

How does Aromatherapy Work?

Aromatherapy activates your nose's smell receptors, which send messages directly to your limbic system in the brain. You are affected by your limbic system when it comes to emotions, memory, learning, appetite, and sexual drive. 

Different bodily responses are stimulated when essential oils are inhaled, including breathing patterns and blood pressure.

Aromatherapy can be used to treat a wide range of mental and physical conditions. There are essential oils that can ease pain, increase focus, enhance your sense of smell, promote restful sleep, or aid digestion. 

Direct inhalation, vaporizers, humidifiers, perfumes, and aromatherapy diffusers are some of how aromatherapy can be used.

Since essential oils are capable of performing multiple functions, you can create (or find) a blend that will satisfy your mental and physical health needs by knowing the benefits of each.

How Essential Oils are used

According to one theory, aromatherapy works by stimulating the smell receptors in your nose, which then send signals to your brain. The body's chemical and energy systems can also be affected by essential oils.

Consequently, aromatherapy is often used to treat anxiety and stress as a natural remedy. Aromatherapy uses essential oils topically and inhaled.

Despite claims on the internet, essential oils should never be ingested. Essential oils aren't safe to swallow because there isn't enough research on them. 

Aromatherapy for Anxiety

In times of uncertainty, people often experience anxiety. There are nearly 40 million American adults who suffer from anxiety, according to the Anxiety and Depression Association of America. According to studies, people who use aromatherapy to address their anxiety symptoms experience less pain and depression than those who do not. 

An essential oil blend consisting of lavender, bergamot, and frankincense was used in a study by the American College of Healthcare Sciences to massage patients' hands for one week. 

When compared to massage alone, this essential oil blend has stronger healing power when it comes to pain and depression management, and patients reported less pain and depression. 

When you're trying to calm down, you can create fragrant stress relievers in your kitchen. Our sense of smell has the power to evoke vivid memories as a result of aromatherapy.

A common practice among adults, aromatherapy relieves headaches, relieves stress, boosts mood, and improves and prevents many health conditions. Children can also benefit from aromatherapy, which many people are unaware of. 

You can provide your child with an exceptionally beneficial experience by using aromatherapy products like the Aroma Sense shower head. The benefits of aromatherapy are countless, and it's all natural.

At-Home Aromatherapy

There are several ways you can use aromatherapy at home to relax:

  • Fill a room with scent by placing essential oils in an infuser.
  • About 2 cups of water should be infused with essential oil. Dip a washcloth in the water and stir. Wipe your face, hands, and neck with the cloth after wringing it out. 
  • You can also keep the clothes in the refrigerator for later use. A few drops of the essential oil will do. Check the strength of the fragrance with one or two. 
  • Make your skin smell good by applying a scented lotion.
  • Prepare a scented stick. Keep a few in your purse or pocket for emergencies.

The Best Essential Oils for Anxiety

1. Valerian

In ancient times, Valerian was used for its medicinal properties. Valerian essential oil has a woody, earthy, or musky scent and comes from the roots of the plant. It may be unpleasant to some individuals.

According to some studies, Valerian contains compounds that promote sleep and calm the nervous system. The effects can be mildly sedative. This is why it is commonly used as a sleep aid.

2. Lavender

Aromatherapy oils such as lavender are very popular. An undertone of the woody or herbal scent accompanies the sweet floral scent.

Anxiety can be calmed with lavender oil. Additionally, it has a sedative effect and may help with sleep problems, especially if you are experiencing stress or anxiety.

3. Jasmine

Often used in perfumes and cosmetic products, jasmine oil has a gorgeous floral scent. Teas may also be flavored with jasmine. Romance and well-being can be promoted by inhaling jasmine oil.

Jasmine oil calms the nervous system without causing sleepiness, unlike some other essential oils used for anxiety. Some people may experience a stimulant effect from it.

4. Vetiver

Although vetiver is not as widely known as other essential oils, it is no less effective. It is sometimes called khus oil. India's grassy vetiver plant produces vetiver oil. The scent is sweet and earthy.

Sleep can be improved with vetiver oil since it helps calm the nervous system. Stress and anxiety may also be eased through it.

Research into vetiver and anxiety in humans is limited, as with other essential oils we have discussed. Animal studies, however, have shown that it can reduce anxiety.

The Bottom Line

Stress or anxiety triggers the release of a stress hormone called cortisol in our bodies. Aromatherapy, under normal conditions can reduce inflammation, blood pressure, and regulate blood sugar. 

We can, however, experience anxiety, depression, and other health problems when we are under too much stress. Aromatherapy reduces anxiety and cortisol levels in participants. 

An aromatherapy session might be just what you need if you have a stressful day at work or an important appointment. However, if you experience chronic anxiety that interferes with your daily activities, you should seek professional help. Your management plan can be tailored to your needs by them.

Leaving summer behind with backyard barbecues, impromptu pool parties, and watermelon so ripe and juicy isn't easy.

Diffusing and blending warming essential oils such as ginger, cardamom, cinnamon, and clove are perfect for the cooler autumn temperatures and colorful falling leaves.

What is Aromatherapy?

The use of essential oils for therapeutic purposes is known as aromatherapy. The use of aromatherapy dates back thousands of years. 

The scent molecules in essential oils travel directly into the brain from the olfactory nerves, primarily influencing the amygdala, which controls emotions.

The skin is also capable of absorbing essential oils. Wintergreen oil may be added to massage oil to relax tight muscles. Lavender can be added to bath salts to create a soothing bath experience.

What Aromatherapy Scents are Good For?

The effectiveness of aromatherapy scents in human health has not been adequately explored, despite claims they are natural remedies for several ailments. 

Several studies have shown that aromatherapy scents can kill Lyme bacteria more effectively than antibiotics, but results from human clinical trials have been mixed.

They seem to be beneficial in some studies, but not in others. The effectiveness of aromatherapy scents has been tested in clinical trials for conditions such as:

  • Insomnia
  • Depression
  • Dry mouth
  • Anxiety
  • Nausea
  • Low appetite

Pure essential oils are concentrated liquids derived from the leaves, roots, flowers, and bark of plants. They contain aromatic and beneficial compounds that work harmoniously with the body. 

You will feel refreshed and energized after indulging in our choice of fragrances. Choose from lemon citrus, minty eucalyptus, and lavender stress-free options. 

Health and well-being have been supported by them for centuries. The best Aromatherapy Scents for the Fall season include:

1. Lemon

Improves alertness, concentration, and detoxifies the skin. Antioxidants in lemon oil help to rejuvenate and detoxify the skin. Various skin disorders and pimples can be treated with its antiseptic properties. 

The aromatherapy benefits of lemon include improved concentration, increased awareness, and an increase in energy. In addition to reducing anxiety and insomnia symptoms, it is used by many experts to reduce stress and anxiety.

2. Vanilla

Aromatherapy enhances relaxation and reduces stress by providing an uplifting scent. Free radicals are neutralized by vanilla oil's antioxidant properties. 

Additionally, vanilla is often used as a stress, anxiety, and hypersensitive nerve relaxant. The most important benefit of vanilla is that it suppresses depression.

3. Citrus mango

Skin is moisturized, signs of aging are slowed, and immunity is boosted. In addition to improving digestive health, mango oil has a high concentration of antioxidants and can be used as a skin moisturizer. Dry, cracked skin can be moisturized and protected with its hydrating and healing properties.

4. Eucalyptus

This substance stimulates the respiratory system, treats wounds, relieves mental exhaustion, reduces muscle pain, and treats skin infections. The properties of eucalyptus oil include antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and decongestant properties. 

Colds, coughs, runny noses, sore throats, asthma, and nasal congestion can be treated with it. It stimulates mental activity, increases blood flow to the brain, and relieves fatigue and sluggishness in aromatherapy.

5. Lavender

Anxiety can be calmed, sleep can be improved, blood circulation can be improved, acne can be treated, and the immune system can be strengthened. In addition to treating migraines and headaches, lavender oil also relieves depression, nervous tension, and emotional stress. As well as inhibiting acne-causing bacteria, it regulates sebum production. Aromatherapy uses it to induce sleep to treat insomnia and anxiety.

6. Jasmine

This plant is great for aphrodisiacs, sleep aids, and skin hydration. As well as providing relief from coughs, jasmine oil can also help eliminate snoring by clearing out phlegm in the respiratory tracts. Dehydrated, dry and brittle skin can be treated with it. 

Jasmine is widely known in aromatherapy for its ability to increase libido and feelings of sexual desire, and for its ability to put people in the mood for love. By encouraging positive and constructive emotions, it calms down the body, mind, and soul.

7. Vitamin C

By neutralizing chlorine on contact, the Vitamin C cartridge prevents dry skin and hair. Skin elasticity and collagen production are enhanced by vitamin C.

How Beneficial are Aromatherapy Scents for Fall

These aromatherapy scents for fall offer various benefits such as:

  • Chlorine neutralization
    •

    By neutralizing chlorine on contact, the Vitamin C cartridge prevents dryness of your skin and hair. The production of collagen depends on vitamin C, which helps maintain skin elasticity.

  • Micro fabric filtration

    Pipe residue and unwanted contaminants will not be able to pass through the microfiber filter, allowing only particle-free water to pass.

  • Water pressure boost

    Aroma Sense shower head is designed to optimize water pressure 1.5x more than a well branded shower head.

  • Negative ions

    Compared to a standard shower, our innovative one produces four times more negative ions. Natural negative ions such as waterfalls are highly concentrated in nature and have been scientifically proven to promote blood flow, relieve stress, balance pH, and promote breathing.

    General Safety Information

    Undiluted essential oils, absolutes, CO2s, or other concentrated essences should not be taken internally or applied to the skin without advanced knowledge of essential oils or consulting a qualified aromatherapist. 

    Pregnant women, epileptics, people with liver damage, cancer patients, and those with other medical conditions should use oils with the guidance of a qualified aromatherapist. 

    Always dilute oils for children according to the recommended dilution ratios before using them. 

    Using oils with children, the elderly, or if you are taking medications should be discussed with a qualified aromatherapy practitioner. Carefully read the safety information page before using this or any essential oil.

How Aromatherapy Can Ease Stress & Anxiety

Posted by Matthew Eng on November 14, 2021

When life gets hectic, it can be difficult for us to slow down and simply relax. As a result, we can build up stress and anxiety over time. One of the most effective and convenient ways to ease stress and anxiety is through aromatherapy, which is the practice of inhaling or topically applying essential oils to promote well-being. For hundreds of years, aromatherapy has been used to treat various psychological and physical ailments. Now, it’s known that essential oils stimulate smell receptors in the nose and activate parts of the brain that play a role in regulating emotions and can cause other psychological effects. While there is still ongoing research on aromatherapy, studies so far have shown that it can help with stress and anxiety in the following ways:

Reduces stress response in the body

When we’re stressed or anxious, our body reacts to this event by releasing a stress hormone called cortisol. Under normal circumstances, this chemical helps us with reducing inflammation, blood pressure, regulating blood sugar, and many other natural functions. However, when we’re under too much stress, it can lead to anxiety, depression, and a number of other health problems. A 2016 study found that aromatherapy with lavender helped reduce anxiety and cortisol levels in participants. If you’re looking for some stress relief, then Aroma Sense has got your back! Incorporate lavender into your daily routine with the Aroma Sense Vitamin C cartridge infused with lavender, which can be used with one of our many filtered shower heads.

No matter how your sleep is disrupted, it can be a recipe for disaster. Sleep is one of the most important aspects of our daily life and health. Without it, you can experience headaches, inability to focus, significant fatigue, and irritability. Aromatherapy can help with improving sleep as a result of reducing stress and other contributing factors. Lemon essential oil is known to have sedative and anxiety-reducing properties that help with promoting better sleep. You can smell this refreshing and uplifting aroma with one of our Vitamin C cartridges that contain lemon essential oil. Not only will you experience the benefits of aromatherapy in your shower, but you will also come out squeaky clean!

Takeaway

As you can already tell by now, our sense of smell is incredibly powerful. It causes physical and mental changes in our body that can have rippling effects on every part of our life. Using aromatherapy, we can quickly and easily change how we feel no matter the circumstance. As a result of reducing stress and anxiety, essential oils also help us to relax and feel calmer. bodyHtml:
Tips For New Aromatherapy Users

Posted by Matthew Eng on November 14, 2021

If you’re new to the world of aromatherapy, it can feel a bit overwhelming getting started. Don’t worry, we’re here to help! The good news is that aromatherapy can be as easy or as hard as you want it to be. It’s a truly personal experience for everyone, and it can also be fun! Continue reading to learn more about how you can enhance your life with aromatherapy.

What are essential oils?

Essential oils are concentrated mixtures made from different parts of plants like leaves, seeds, or roots. Plants contain a lot of different chemicals that are not only good for plants, but are also good for people too. However, it takes a lot of plants to make even one bottle of essential oil. For example, you need about 250 pounds of lavender flowers to make 1 pound of lavender essential oil. While it might seem like a lot, it shows that many plants are needed to make effective botanical oils.

What is aromatherapy?

People have been practicing aromatherapy for hundreds of years, which involves smelling essential oils for health benefits. Research is still ongoing on the effectiveness of aromatherapy and essential oils, but the results so far provide evidence that the practice can potentially affect our mental state and well-being. Experts believe that the aromas we inhale from the essential oils travel from our nose and directly to the brain, where it targets and stimulates areas responsible for our emotions. Aromatherapy can be done by smelling the essential oils straight from the bottle, using a diffuser, or inhaling them from a bowl of hot water.

The dos and don’ts

Now that we know how helpful aromatherapy can be, let’s dive into how we can use essential oils properly and effectively.

  • DO use them if you’re stressed. Essential oils like lavender are known to help you relax and destress. You can use them to help you before, during, or after particular rough times. Aromatherapy isn’t a cure-all, but it can help take the edge off.
  • DON’T use just any essential oil. Although essential oils are made out of plants, this fact can be a bit misleading for most. They have the potential to cause irritation or allergic reactions in some people. Just like any other medication or topical you buy, you should test a little bit of the oil on a small area of your skin to see how you react before you commit to using it.
  • DO read the labels. Because the formulation of essential oils can vary from manufacturer to manufacturer, it is highly recommended that you pick manufacturers that are transparent on the oil’s source. Look for labels that detail the plant’s botanical name and the part of the plant used.
  • DON’T use edible oils. Even if an oil is safe to eat, that doesn’t mean it’s safe to apply to your skin. In fact, it may cause damage, such as blisters or burns. This applies the other way around too! Essential oils are great for smelling or rubbing into your skin but are not so great when ingested and can even cause serious health complications.

Best Essential Oils for The Holidays

Posted by Matthew Eng on November 11, 2021

With the holiday season quickly coming up, many of us are starting to gear up our homes for the coming festivities. Christmas trees, ornaments, and décor are on most people’s list to pull out of the closet. However, one of the best ways to set the mood is by making your home smell like Christmas! Continue reading to see the best essential oils to use to get the cozy winter and holiday vibes at home.

  1. Nothing screams Christmas trees like the scent of pine. Whether you have a real tree or not, you can make your house smell like one with pine oil. This invigorating aroma is known to help stimulate metabolism, reduce stress, treat respiratory problems, and relieve pain. This is a great scent to complement your holiday dinners! If you’re looking to get into the holiday spirit first thing in the morning, try the Aroma Sense Vitamin C cartridge infused with pine essential oil!

 

  1. Citrus Mango. Guess what else we ring in during the holidays? That’s right! Citrus season! It’s also no surprise that citrus scents are popular during this time of year. You can add a bit of sweetness to your home with the Aroma Sense Vitamin C cartridge with citrus mango! The citrus and mango combo will not only help to reinvigorate you during your morning (or evening) showers, but it can also help in alleviating digestive conditions and in moisturizing the skin.
  1. While lavender is known for being a summer floral, it is still a great all-around scent to have, especially when it’s during a busy season like the holidays. Lavender can help you relax and de-stress before and after a long week celebrating with the family. One of the best and easiest ways to experience lavender is with the Aroma Sense Aromatherapy showerheads, along with the lavender-infused vitamin C cartridge.

 

  1. Whenever you hear someone say that something smells like nostalgia, peppermint has got to be one of those scents that brings most of us back in time. This classic scent can be found in many of our favorite childhood treats, including cookies and candy canes. Use peppermint oil to not only relive your childhood memories but to also boost your energy and promote relaxation!

 

  1. If you want your home to feel extra cozy, cinnamon oil is the way to go! Just like peppermint, cinnamon is one of those scents that remind us of the holiday season while growing up. Most classic holiday treats have cinnamon in them, including eggnog and gingerbread cookies. Not only will it add some spice to your home, but it also can benefit your health in several ways. Cinnamon is known for being anti-inflammatory and anti-bacterial and is an antioxidant.

 

Need some extra cheer in your life? Transform your shower routine with the Aroma Sense collection of shower heads with Vitamin C cartridges infused with pine, citrus mango, and lavender! Our products will turn your bathroom into the ultimate home spa with aromatherapy and a relaxing atmosphere.

Vitamin C is one of the most important nutrients for our bodies, both inside and out. It has many benefits, but one of the most astounding is how crucial it is in the production of collagen. Collagen is an essential protein in our bodies that contributes to the elasticity and firmness of our skin. Vitamin C works to improve skin texture and tone, as well as hydrate your skin. It speeds up the renewal of our skin cells, potentially reducing DNA damage, and strengthens our blood vessels. Vitamin C also neutralizes free radicals, reducing and reversing skin damage. Talk about a powerhouse of a nutrient! With all of these amazing benefits, it was essential to us that we incorporated vitamin C into our Aroma Sense showerheads so that no matter which scent you choose, you can enjoy the benefits it offers!

We use L-ascorbic acid in our Aroma Sense showerheads, which is a form of vitamin C that will penetrate through the layers of your skin. So how does it work exactly? Our showerheads are simple to set up. You just replace your existing showerhead with it! Everything you need for a luxurious shower experience is already included in the showerhead itself, so there is no special setup needed. Once the showerhead is installed and you turn on the water, the process starts. Water flows past the vitamin C cartridge, initiating a reaction that effectively eliminates chlorine and releases the vitamin C benefits. This step also stimulates the aromatherapy oils to be released! Once it’s past this cartridge, it flows through the ceramic beads to kill bacteria. It is then filtered using a microfiber filter to pull out contaminants. As a final luxurious step, the design of the triangular spray plate increases the water pressure by a satisfying 1.5x what it normally is. This unique design also increases the negative ions in the water to increase blood flow, relieve stress, balance pH, and facilitate breathing for overall mental clarity and well-being.

The physical benefits of a vitamin C filtered shower are wonderful, but we don’t stop with that! The ceramic beads and microfiber filter ensure that your water is as clean as possible. Any sediment from the shower pipes is filtered out, as well as and heavy metals, fluoride, iron or rust. The result is an amazingly spa-like shower experience right at home, with noticeably softer skin and hair. With time and consistent use, you may even notice an increase in skin elasticity, firmness, and fewer wrinkles! Not only that, but you will emerge from your shower feeling rejuvenated! Depending on which scent cartridge you use, you will feel energized and ready to take on the day, or refreshed and ready for a relaxed, deep sleep. The best part is, you can switch from one to the other with a quick cartridge change. Once you try a vitamin C aromatherapy shower, you won’t go back to anything else!

bodyHtml:
How Aromatherapy Can Help You

Posted by Matthew Eng on September 29, 2021

What is aromatherapy and how can it help you? Aromatherapy is the practice of inhaling the scent of aromatic essential oils from a variety of plants. It has been used for thousands of years for a wide range of purposes, and by people from every country. The reason it is so effective is because our sense of smell is directly connected to the limbic system, which is a part of our brain that is responsible for sending a chemical message to our nervous system. Aromatherapy is often associated with luxury, but there are many health benefits to using it as well. Here are a few benefits you may notice when you begin using aromatherapy:

 

It can help relieve anxiety and promote relaxation

Evident in any spa around the globe, this is the most common use of aromatherapy. Many different scents can be used to help take away the stress of the day: lemon, lavender, and jasmine to name a few. These oils are known to be effective in soothing your mind and balancing your mood. Put one of these scent cartridges into your aromatherapy shower head and enjoy the most relaxing shower of your life!

 

It can boost energy and promote focus

The second most popular use for aromatherapy is to give you a boost of energy so you can start your day right! It won’t just give you a boost of energy though, the right scents can keep your mind from wandering, racing, or getting distracted. Bonus: by using aromatherapy to boost your energy instead of an excess of other stimulants such as energy drinks, you can avoid the jittery side effects! Try using our lemon, citrus mango or eucalyptus cartridge and say goodbye to that midday slump!

 

It can relieve pain and promote healing

Eucalyptus and lavender are sure to become one of your favorite scents if you suffer from headaches, a sensitive immune system, or inflammation. These scents are known to stimulate oxygen and blood flow to the areas of your body that need it most, and can even boost your immune system with their antimicrobial properties. They are known to provide relief for some skin conditions too!

It can help you sleep better

There is no doubt that all of us are in need of a good night’s sleep. Aromatherapy can ease you into such a deep state of relaxation that it can lull you into a deep sleep. It can even promote the re-regulation of your circadian rhythm over time. If you struggle with not being able to get a restful sleep, commit to using lavender for 15 days and see how your rest improves!

Are you ready to combine the therapeutic benefits of aromatherapy with the luxurious experience of a spa, right at home? Start with the Aroma Sense Starter Pack, and add any of the scent cartridges. You can switch the scent cartridges out based on the experience you are looking for!

bodyHtml:
How Microfiber Filters Protect You from Rust & Contaminants

Posted by Matthew Eng on July 29, 2021

When you’re taking a shower, you would think that you’re safe and protected. This is the only time in your daily life when you’re completely vulnerable and shut off from the rest of the world. But it could actually be harming you more than it is helping you. Although you may not notice it, your shower water could contain harmful chemicals that can negatively impact your health. Luckily, microfiber filters can help you get on your way toward a healthier lifestyle. In this article, we’ll discuss why your current showerhead isn’t cutting it and what microfiber filters can do for you.

What’s wrong with my current showerhead?

Do you know where your shower water comes from? If you guessed water treatment centers, then you’re right. What you may not know is by what means they treat the water you submerge yourself in every day. Chorine is typically used to disinfect our water supplies and is effective at reducing the bacteria in our drinking water. But what’s unfortunate is that this chemical is incredibly harmful to our bodies. Because it’s a disinfectant, it has the potential to damage our intestinal flora, also known as our good bacteria. It is a powerful antimicrobial and can kill several strains of bacteria. Studies have also shown that using chlorinated water can lead to increased risk of bladder, rectal, and kidney cancers.

Additionally, your current showerhead may not be doing a very good job at filtering out other particles that lurk in your water. You might have noticed that your hair tends to become dry, brittle, and frizzy after showering. What is not accounted for at water treatment centers are the rust, lead, heavy metals, and other contaminants that could come from residue in your pipes. While they’re generally safe to shower in, they can dry out your hair and skin.

How do microfiber filters protect me from rust and other contaminants?

It’s common practice to filter drinking water, so it’s not that hard to believe that we should filter our shower water too. There are many different types of shower filters out there, but microfiber filters stand out above the rest because of their convenience, versatility, and effectiveness. They are designed to trap rust, dirt, and other particles in your water. What’s also great is that you can replace them after each use. Many people who have made the switch are shocked to find out the number of contaminants they have exposed themselves to. However, they are also glad that they are on their way to a healthier lifestyle and find that it is like coming to a luxury spa every day.

Start on your journey to cleaner water today with the Aroma Sense Aromatherapy Shower Head! Not only will you be able to benefit from aromatherapy, but you will also find overall improvement in your health. Each showerhead contains a microfiber filter and Vitamin C shower cartridge that neutralizes chlorine, removes contaminants, and bathes you in Vitamin C for healthier hair and skin.

How Essential Oils Improve Your Quality of Life

Posted by Matthew Eng on July 29, 2021

There is nothing more powerful than your sense of smell, and it is no surprise that it makes a significant impact on your well-being. If you’re looking to improve your quality of life, then aromatherapy is a great place to start. Aromatherapy uses essential oils to promote physical and mental health. Essential oils contain highly concentrated compounds that are unique to each plant they come from and offer many different benefits. Here, we’ll show you how essential oils can improve your quality of life.

Clears and moisturizes your skin

For many of us, we’ve been led to believe that the answer to our acne and other skin problems lies in the hundreds of cosmetic products and facial regimens sold out there. However, that’s not entirely the case. While your skin condition is unique to you as a person, it can also significantly benefit from aromatherapy. Essential oils such as lavender can help you with inflammation, fine lines, and dry skin without the need for extra skincare products.

Reduces use of commercial products

Along the same lines, you’ll begin to realize that you didn’t need as many skincare or other products as you previously thought. And you might even start to become more conscious of what you buy. You’ll think twice about whether or not certain products are safe for you and your family. Finding the right essential oil will change your mindset and your life for the better.

Sleepless nights will be a thing of the past

If you’re having difficulty falling asleep at night, essential oils could help. Many people use essential oils for this very reason. Aromatherapy promotes relaxation in both mind and body and keeps you asleep for the rest of the night. Your whole life will change just by getting more sleep and adding aromatherapy to your routine. One of the best essential oils for sleep is jasmine, which is known for tackling insomnia. Jasmine contains botanical compounds that work similarly to prescribed sleep medications.

Helps you prioritize your mental health

While essential oils are not a cure for mental illness, they can certainly help. Several of them have been shown to combat symptoms of depression and anxiety. You might find yourself with a more positive outlook, less tension, and an uplifted spirit. Your self-esteem and confidence will soar. With the help of aromatherapy and conventional treatment, you’ll be on your way to a happier life.

Enhances every aspect of your life

Not only will all of the above get an upgrade, but all aspects of your life will too. Getting out of bed won’t be so dreadful anymore. That workout you keep pushing off? You’ll conquer it in no time! Lemon oil will give you the energy boost and mental clarity you need to take on the world.

One of the best ways to enhance your life and integrate essential oils into your routine is through your daily shower. With the Aroma Sense Aromatherapy Showerhead, it is now easier than ever. bodyHtml:
Benefits of Morning Showers

Posted by Matthew Eng on July 29, 2021

Whether you’re a night owl or always burning the midnight oil, mornings can feel like a struggle. One of the best ways to kickstart your day is with a morning shower. Of course, we shower to keep ourselves clean, but did you know that it can help with your energy, mood, and productivity? Keep reading to see how you can benefit from a morning shower.

Reduces stress

We all deal with some kind of stress in our lives, and it can really take a toll on our health over time. For some of us, our only form of self-care is a trip to the shower every day. Fortunately, morning showers can help improve your mental health by reducing symptoms of depression and anxiety naturally. It can also serve as a healthy break from the daily hustle and bustle. You can further boost this relaxing vibe with lavender in an aromatherapy shower head. Lavender is known to help remedy stress and release negative emotions because of its soothing and calming scent.

Boosts energy

If you’re just not feeling it in the morning, a cold morning shower will quickly turn that around. While it is not the most pleasant way to wake up, it sure works! Research has found that cold showers stimulate your nervous system, which helps you to become more alert. In response to the cold temperature, your body reduces the amount of melatonin (sleep hormone) and increases your blood circulation/heart rate/breathing rate, leading you to feeling more awake. This strategy is so powerful that it is equivalent to having a cup of coffee in the morning. Aromatherapy with eucalyptus is great to get you going first thing in the morning.

Improves mood

Starting your day off on the right note has a significant effect on how you feel for the rest of it. For one, feeling clean instantly boosts your norepinephrine and serotonin levels. These hormones are like an espresso shot of energy and happiness, which is definitely needed in the morning. Additionally, you’ll also feel better about yourself. You’ll have more confidence to seize the day and keep yourself on track. The best aromatherapy pick-me-ups are citrus mango and lemon. They both work to improve your mood, counter symptoms of depression, and reduce anxiety.

Fights infections

The key to a great life is equally great health. When you take a shower, not only are you keeping clean, but you are also washing away all of the germs that could make you sick. Morning showers have also been shown to help your body produce white blood cells, which are crucial to your body’s defense system. Adding aromatherapy with jasmine to your shower will be extremely powerful in fighting off potential infections. Inhalation

How to Maintain Your Aroma Sense Shower Head

Posted by Matthew Eng on May 05, 2021

Shower heads are one of the last places you’d think of to clean. We often mistakenly think that they can self-clean. However, shower heads are also prone to build up, just like the rest of our shower. If you’ve recently installed an Aroma Sense shower head into your shower, the work doesn’t stop there. To keep it functioning at full capacity, you need to regularly maintain it over time. Here, we’ll go over the maintenance required for your wall-mounted or handheld Aroma Sense shower head.

Replacing the vitamin C cartridge

If you no longer smell the fragrance from the shower head or you see that the cartridge is clear, then it might be time to replace the vitamin C cartridge. Usually, this needs to be done every 90 days for the wall-mounted shower head and every 45 days for the handheld model depending on usage. To replace the cartridge in both types of shower head units, you first want to twist the head counterclockwise while holding either the body of the unit or the handle. Then, take out the old cartridge and replace it with the new one. For the handheld shower head cartridge, you will notice that it is labeled with “In” and “Out” on the side. Make sure that the “In” section goes into the shower head first. Once you have reassembled the shower head, turn on the faucet to check for any leakages.

Increasing output of the vitamin C cartridge

You can increase the strength of the fragrance to mask any odors or fill a larger bathroom with the smell. To do this, you need to remove the vitamin C cartridge from the shower head. Using a thumbtack or sharp object, punch a larger hole where the premade hole is on top of the cartridge. When you have your desired size hold, reinsert the cartridge back into the shower head in the correct position until secure. Turn the faucet on and test it out to see if the strength of the fragrance is enough for you. You can continue to gradually increase the size of the hole until you are happy with the smell.

Cleaning the microfiber filter and spray plate

If you find that the shower head spray seems off or the water flow is inconsistent, there may be an issue with the microfiber filter and spray plate. They should be cleaned regularly to keep your filtration system functioning normally. The process for cleaning these two parts is the same in both the wall-mount and handheld shower heads. First, open the showerhead cap by turning it counterclockwise. Separate the shower head spray plate, shower cap rubber O-ring, and microfiber filter. Under running water, clean the microfiber filter while using your finger to remove any dirt and debris. This filter usually needs to be replaced after 2-3 washes if it a rust-like color. Continue to clean the spray plate with vinegar or dishwasher detergent. Afterward, reassemble the pieces back together into the shower head and place them back onto the unit.

Getting spare parts

Along with regularly maintaining the above parts, we also recommend that you monitor the rest of the shower head unit on a consistent basis for any signs of leakage, damage, or cracks. If it is something you cannot fix, then you may need to replace them. You can easily find all of the spare parts of our shower head units on the Aroma Sense website.

Monitoring, cleaning, and working on the Aroma Sense Aromatherapy Shower Head is like a form of self-care. The extra care you take to regularly maintain your shower head will go a long way in not only keeping the device working for longer, but also will help you on your journey to better health.

Showering after a workout is incredibly beneficial for you for multiple reasons. Here are some of the reasons why you should hit the showers after your workout. 

Aids with Recovery

Showering after a workout has been proven to help your muscles recover faster and helps your body able to bounce back and be able to do another workout. 

This is because during you’re shower it assists in relieving all the lactic acid out of your muscles which causes you to be sore the day after. 

Should I Take A Cold or Hot Shower

Taking a cold or hot shower will depend on your preferences and level of comfortability. What is recommended, is to take a cold and hot shower at the same time. Now this means that you will first start with cold water.

The reason why you want to start with cold water is due to the ability it has to reduce the inflammation of muscles, joints, and tendons. 

It reduces inflammation when the cold water comes in contact with your skin, it's able to decrease the blood flow locally. 

After the cold shower, you want to switch it to hot or warm water.

This will now improve the muscle and joint recovery time and flush out any inflammatory cells your body has inside. 

If you ever come out of leg day without the ability to walk properly it's because you’re sore, then try the cold-to-hot shower method next time you hit the showers. 

This will help with improving your body’s mobility so the stiffness after the workout does not happen. 

It Improves Your Hygiene

Coming out of the gym is a great feeling but what's not a great feeling is the odor you have once you come out of the gym. 

Even with using deodorant and cologne, the smell may still linger, and you don’t want to go to work or your next date smelling bad. 

Post workout showers improves hygiene by removing all the sweat, oil, & dirt you accumulated throughout your workout to keep your skin looking refreshed and healthy. You want to wait 10 minutes after your workout to shower so that you give yourself ample time to stretch and let your body recover after you exercise. 

Prevents Clogged Pores

When you sweat, you begin to collect a lot of bacteria and skin cells. Most of the time, they will just get stuck in your pores.

Some people have experienced that showering with cold or cool water reduces the number of sick days they have used for work.

This is due to the reduction of lactic acid inside your body and eliminating the leftover sweat and bacteria from the workout.

5. It Will Get the Germs Off Your Bed

Laying down on your bed without washing your face or showering can transfer the germs and dirt you have on your skin to the pillow or bed. 

If this happens then even if you clean yourself the germs and dirt may still remain on the bed. 

Your head especially contains a lot of bacteria and if you don’t shower your hair, it will contaminate the pillow and may give your face acne. 

Whether you want that extra 20 minutes of sleep that everyone wants before they go to work or even healthier skin, showering at night will help you improve your health and skin. title: Winter Beauty Tips & Tricks
excerpt: As the weather gets colder and the days get shorter, you might enjoy a little boost from mixing things up. Or maybe you want a new look for the holidays or just need to adapt to the season. Either way, there are lots of tweaks you can make to easily winterize your routine and your look this season.
author: Customer Service
bodyHtml:
Winter Beauty Tips & Tricks

Posted by Customer Service on November 25, 2019

As the weather gets colder and the days get shorter, you might enjoy a little boost from mixing things up. Or maybe you want a new look for the holidays or just need to adapt to the season. Either way, there are lots of tweaks you can make to easily winterize your routine and your look this season.

Use an exfoliating scrub.

When the weather gets cold and windy, the air will dry out your skin, leaving it flaky and chapped. The most important step in preventing dry skin is using an exfoliating scrub to slough off dead skin cells, on both your face and body. For most people, exfoliating once or twice a week is enough (and doing it more can irritate your skin).

Moisturize regularly.

Once you’ve exfoliated, the next step to combatting winter dryness is moisturizing. It’s important to moisturize every day, especially in the winter, and it’s best done right after showering. You might even want to moisturize both in the morning and at night.

Use gentle products on your face.

Dry winter skin is also easily irritated, and harsh face products will only make it worse. If you notice your skin getting red or feeling uncomfortable, try switching to gentler products. Look for cleansers and moisturizers made from all-natural ingredients or designed specifically for sensitive skin. You might also want to use peels or deep-cleansing masks more sparingly this time of year.

Don’t forget the sunscreen.

It’s easy to relegate sunscreen to summer hikes and beach vacations, but sunburns can also happen during the winter. It’s just as important to wear sunscreen on cold days, especially on your face.

Make sure to use conditioner.

The cold air also tends to leave hair dry and frizzy, which can mean you’re constantly battling fly-aways. To keep them under control, make sure you don’t skip the hair conditioner whenever you shampoo.

Experiment with darker nail polish.

When it comes to manicures and pedicures, we tend to go with pastels or brighter colors in the spring and summer. But as the weather transitions, it’s time to transition your nails as well. As it gets cold out, start looking for darker colors like deep red or crimson.

Go for bright whites and pale blues.

On the other hand, colors that reflect the snowy weather also make perfect winter nails. This is the time for clean, stark white or pale, icy blue. And that doesn’t just go for nails. Shadows in shimmery versions of these colors will create a great wintry eye look as well.

Invest in some scarves.

Scarves are one of the best accessories for winter. Adding a scarf is an easy way to stay warm, and it’ll dress up almost any outfit. Plus, a chunky soft one will give you that cozy feeling we all crave when the weather gets cold. Pick up some scarves in a couple different colors, or go for one with a bold pattern to make a simple outfit really pop.

Of course, your ideal winter beauty routine and overall look will depend on your specific skin and style, but these tips should help get you started for the season.

So as the weather gets colder, start using these tips when you shower. Take shorter showers. Cold winter air is a major cause
author: Customer Service
bodyHtml:
How to Take Showers in the winter

Posted by Customer Service on November 18, 2019

Taking a shower probably doesn’t seem like something you need guidelines for. But to stay comfortable and healthy in the winter, there are actually a few things to consider. So as the weather gets colder, start using these tips when you shower.

Take shorter showers.

Cold winter air is a major cause of dry, irritated skin, so your beauty routine needs to be gentler and more moisturizing to compensate. While it might seem counter-intuitive, getting your skin wet actually dries it out further. The first step to combatting dry skin? Take shorter showers. As a bonus, you’ll save water, too.

Don’t shower excessively.

Similarly, you might consider whether you really need a shower every day – many people don’t, especially in the winter. Depending on your body, skin type, and level of activity, you might be able to get away with skipping a couple days a week. Use that extra time to do something more interesting!

Use cooler water.

While water dries out your skin, hot water dries it out more (even if it feels good at the time). Try showering in slightly cooler water instead to keep your skin happier. Plus, if you gradually turn the temperature down toward the end of your shower, the cold air when you pull back the curtain won’t feel nearly as frigid. You’ll save energy and cut down on your heat bill, too.

Wash with a loofah.

Taking the steps above will keep the dryness from getting even worse, but you’re still likely to experience some level of dry skin. You’ll need some tools to combat it, starting with a loofah, which will slough off dead skin cells. If you don’t already have one, the beginning of winter is the time to switch.

Switch away from bar soap.

Bar soap doesn’t work great with a loofah anyway, and it’s also notoriously drying. Liquid body wash tends to be gentler and more moisturizing, so pick up a bottle to use with your loofah.

Use an exfoliating scrub.

To get rid of all the flaky dead skin cells, washing with a loofah isn’t enough for most people; you really need to use an exfoliating scrub as well. If you don’t want to buy yet another new product, you can even make a scrub yourself by mixing olive or coconut oil with sugar and honey.

Consider splurging on a towel warmer.

Everyone knows how painful those first few seconds after a shower are – when the water’s turned off, you’re still wet, and the air feels frigid. But the one thing that can make it more pleasant is having a warm towel to dry off with. A towel warmer might feel like an extravagant expense, but you (and the rest of your family) will be grateful for it every single time you shower.

As the weather starts to change and you notice your skin feeling a little dry or itchy, try doing these things when you shower to stay more comfortable.

excerpt: People tend to associate travel with summer. School’s out, work tends to slow, and it’s the season of camping, road trips, and beach vacations. But lots of great destinations come alive in the colder months, when they offer unique experiences that you can’t get at other times of the year. Need some
author: Customer Service
bodyHtml:
The most beautiful places to visit this Winter in the US

Posted by Customer Service on November 11, 2019

People tend to associate travel with summer. School’s out, work tends to slow, and it’s the season of camping, road trips, and beach vacations. But lots of great destinations come alive in the colder months, when they offer unique experiences that you can’t get at other times of the year.

Need some wanderlust inspiration? Here are a few of the best wintertime travel spots in the.

Burlington, VT

Vermont has got to be one of the best states to visit in the winter, and Burlington is pretty much the state’s capital of culture and charm. Market Street is the heart of the town, so plan on spending some time strolling and shopping (or window-shopping) there. That’s also where you’ll find Lake Champlain Chocolates, where you can take a free tour, complete with chocolate samples. For other indoor options, check the Flynn Center for frequent performances or catch a film at Roxy Cinema, the town’s locally-owned movie theater. If you’re not afraid of the cold, get out and take a stroll along Lake Champlain, which is gorgeous in the wintertime.

Bozeman, MT

When we talk about places that thrive in the winter, a mountain state like Montana certainly comes in near the top of the list. The college town of Bozeman is the closest town to Big Sky, which was, until recently, the largest ski area in the country. It’s even closer to Bridger Bowl, a popular local hill, and an easy drive to Yellowstone National Park. The park has a peaceful beauty in the winter, when it’s covered in snow and nearly devoid of tourists. In Bozeman itself, you’ll find a charming downtown area, loads of craft breweries and yoga studios, and a hip and diverse dining scene.

New York, NY

In some ways, the Big Apple might be the quintessential U.S. winter destination. The cold doesn’t keep New Yorkers inside, so bundle up and plan to do a lot of walking. Take a stroll through Central Park to enjoy the snow-dusted greenery, or just wander the streets of any of the diverse neighborhoods. While you’re in New York, ice skating is also a must. The rink at Rockefeller Center is iconic, though Wollman Rink in Central Park has a stunning backdrop of the city’s skyline.

Anchorage, AK

For a once-in-a-lifetime winter adventure, consider a trip to Alaska. Its rugged beauty is truly unlike anywhere else in the U.S., and there are so many ways to enjoy it. Anchorage has too many skating rinks and ponds to count, 130 miles of paved bike paths (which are mostly groomed in the winter), and over 100 miles of groomed cross-country skiing trails. Plus, Alaska’s biggest ski area, Alyeska Resort, is only forty miles from town. And perhaps the best reason to make this trip is the Northern Lights, which are frequently visible from right in the city. As Alaska’s biggest city, Anchorage will also give you your pick of performances, museums, spas, and more.

In most places, unless you travel right around the holidays, winter is also the off-season. That means fewer people and lower prices, so you might be able to score a great deal.

excerpt: Every January 1, millions of people set ambitious New Year’s resolutions: exercise more, stop eating sugar, keep their home cleaner. And by the end of the month (or even the week), most of them have given up. While many people fail to keep their resolutions because they were too extreme or they didn
author: Customer Service
bodyHtml:
Why Fall Is a Better Time to Set “New Year’s” Resolutions

Posted by Customer Service on October 21, 2019

Every January 1, millions of people set ambitious New Year’s resolutions: exercise more, stop eating sugar, keep their home cleaner. And by the end of the month (or even the week), most of them have given up. While many people fail to keep their resolutions because they were too extreme or they didn’t have a strategy for meeting them, part of the problem might also be the timing.

Even though a new year seems like the obvious time to make new life changes, it may not be. The only thing that differentiates January 1 from December 31 is the calendar, and a change in the calendar doesn’t magically make it easier to change our lifestyles. However, it might be slightly easier to stick to a resolution at another time of year: the fall.

It’s already a time of transition.

The only transition that comes at the end of December is a gradual shift from cold weather to colder weather. But the beginning of fall is a natural period of transition anyway. For people with children, the start of the school year is a huge shift. At many workplaces, the end of summer brings changes and transitions as well. It also usually marks the end of certain commitments and the beginning of new ones. And as your schedule is already changing, it can be easier to slot in time to work toward your resolutions.

There are no post-holiday blues.

After months of build-up, many people experience sadness, disappointment, or loneliness once the holidays are over. While working toward a goal can help to combat those feelings, they can also make it much harder to stick to a new program, give up something you enjoy, or make other life changes. In the fall, however, you may be feeling a bit happier and more energetic to begin with, making it easier to keep your resolution.

You’ll likely be starting from a healthier place.

Similarly, the holidays are generally a period of indulgence, with events taking place over a stretch of nearly six weeks. Holiday meals and festive treats, the busyness of the season, and the unrelenting weather all make the end of the year an especially unhealthy time for most. Even if your resolution isn’t health-oriented, you’ll be in a better place to tackle it at the end of the summer, which tends to be less stressful and more active than the holiday season.

It’s nicer out.

Lastly, the weather can make a big difference in how easy it is to stick to a new habit, and January is one of the harshest months in most places. Short days, snow and ice, and freezing temperatures make it hard to spend much time outside, and it can just feel easier to stay in. Compare that to early fall, when it’s still pleasant out, maybe even more so than the summer. Start a resolution in September, and you’ll have far fewer obstacles to getting out of the house to keep it.

We all know that New Year’s resolutions are notoriously hard to keep, so why not try something different? Besides, if you start now, you can always use the New Year as a time to reflect, reevaluate, and celebrate the progress you’ve already made.

excerpt: One of the special little things to enjoy during the holiday season is the smell in the air. The scents of the holidays are spicy and woody, minty and sweet. author: Customer Service
bodyHtml:
The best essential oil scents for the holidays

Posted by Customer Service on October 14, 2019

One of the special little things to enjoy during the holiday season is the smell in the air. The scents of the holidays are spicy and woody, minty and sweet. If you just can’t get enough of these warm and inviting smells during the holiday, there’s good news: you can use essential oils to enjoy them non-stop.

If you’re new to the world of essential oils, though, it’s hard to know where to start. These are some of the top oils for the holidays, plus how you can best use them.

Pine

The smell of Christmas trees must be the ultimate holiday scent. If the smell of your tree isn’t strong enough (or your tree is an artificial one), you can create a room spray. Mix some pine essential oil with water in a spray bottle, and spritz it around the house for a boost of Christmas spirit.

Peppermint

Whether they’re for dessert or décor, candy canes say “Christmas” more than almost anything. To enjoy peppermint without the added sugar, simply rub a drop of the oil under your nose. It’s an instant energy booster, too, which we all need during the holiday season.

Frankincense and Myrrh

“Frankincense” and “myrrh” are words that pretty much only come up at Christmastime, and their woody scents are perfect during the holiday season – and they make a perfect complement to each other. The sweet hints of frankincense and the slightly medicinal smell of myrrh make them a great pair to blend together, and both are packed with benefits, including boosting skin health. Add a few drops of both oils to your regular night cream, or mix them together with a little jojoba oil and apply directly to your face. You’ll be able to enjoy the scents and get a nice glow.

Cinnamon

You probably don’t think of cinnamon as an oil, but cinnamon essential oil has been used for centuries for many purposes, including promoting digestion, reducing stress, and boosting immunity. That makes it a potent oil to use during the holiday season. Combine cinnamon essential oil with a little lemon oil to make a holiday-inspired blend for your infuser.

Ginger

Love the smell of freshly-baked gingerbread cookies? You can enjoy the aroma without the calories (or the mess) by using ginger essential oil. Mix it with a citrus oil (like lemon or orange) to make a blend for your diffuser, and set it up in your kitchen. Just don’t blame us when the kids show up expecting cookies!

Clove

The final essential oil that really is essential during the holidays? Clove, with its strong, spicy scent. Among the many benefits of clove oil are its pain-reducing properties. Create a holiday-scented muscle rub by adding a few drops of clove oil to an unscented lotion. You’ll be able to keep getting into the holiday spirit while also easing any joint or muscle pain.

Lastly, of course, essential oils are meant to be blended, and the best holiday-inspired scent might be one you create. Get creative by mixing up your favorite oils until you find the scent that really says “Christmastime” to you.
